intended_object: For a fixed topological group G and a continuous G-equivariant morphism f : X → Y of topological representations, the induced map Hⁿ_cts(G, X) → Hⁿ_cts(G, Y) on continuous group cohomology. Here the cohomology is computed after lifting G and the carriers to the common universe max v w. This comes from the docstring and from the module documentation on universe normalization.
explanation:
The body is Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology.map φ f n`, the map Hⁿ(G, X) ⟶ Hⁿ(H, Y) induced by a pair (φ, f). It is applied with φ the identity continuous group homomorphism of `ULift G`, and with f lifted to the common universe by the `TopRep.uliftFunctor` functor (`normalizedMap f`). So this is ordinary covariant functoriality of continuous cohomology in the coefficients, which is the standard notion.

The universe lift exists only because Mathlib's homogeneous-cochain construction needs the group and the coefficients in one universe. Lifting to ULift is mathematically harmless: up to the evident isomorphisms, ULift G is the same topological group and the lifted representations are the same representations.

The definition is not too narrow. It works for any topological ring k, any topological group G and any morphism of `TopRep`. Fixing the group is the point of a coefficient-functoriality map. The general version that also changes the group is Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology.map`, and this definition is built from it.

The file also proves `normalizedContinuousCohomologyMap_id` and `normalizedContinuousCohomologyMap_comp`, i.e. that the map preserves identities and composition, as a functor should.
